# Canonical Daintree CLI tool wire names — a snapshot of the CLI's tool registry.
#
# Consumed by tests/unit/test_skill_catalog_hygiene.py to check that every skill's
# requiredTools entry names a tool that actually exists. It is a SNAPSHOT on purpose:
# CI does not fetch the cli/ submodule, so a test that read cli/ at runtime would
# silently no-op there (or hard-fail). Snapshot taken against cli/ @ dceef8c.
#
# Format: one wire name per line, sorted, "#" lines are comments. The registry maps
# an internal dotted name to its OpenAI wire name by replacing EVERY "." with "__"
# (cli/internal/tools/registry.go, toWireName): fs.read -> fs__read. Skill frontmatter
# writes requiredTools in the dotted form, so the test normalizes with the same
# substitution before comparing.
#
# REGENERATION. This file is the name-only projection of the full-schema capture at
# benchmarks/_harness/fixtures/cli_tool_inventory.json. Refresh that one first (its
# recipe lives in benchmarks/_harness/fixtures/README.md: populate the pinned cli/
# submodule with `git submodule update --init cli`, build a throwaway main.go inside
# the module tree that registers every tool family with zero-value Deps and prints
# `Registry.OpenAITools(nil)`, then delete the throwaway package), then regenerate
# this file from it, keeping this header:
#
#   python -c "import json;print('\n'.join(sorted(t['function']['name'] for t in json.load(open('benchmarks/_harness/fixtures/cli_tool_inventory.json')))))"
#
# Regenerate when the CLI adds, removes, or renames a tool. The hygiene test asserts
# ONE direction only (every declared requiredTools name appears here); registry tools
# that no skill declares are the normal, expected state.
